claim: For every fixed 0<=p<1/2 the explicit finite no-query procedure has expected true cost at most C_p max(1,ln n) MST(d), for all n>=2 and all metrics and post-mask adversaries.
Anand et al. prove O_p(log n) under arbitrary replacements for p<1/4.
Anand et al. prove a linear obstruction for p>=1/2.
Bateni et al. study the strong/weak distance-oracle model.
Bateni et al. Theorem 4 gives no-strong-query O(sqrt(log n)) MST approximation assuming metric weak observations.
Bateni et al. Appendix F.2.2 Theorem 32 gives a logarithmic obstruction for arbitrary corruptions at p=1/3.
Anand et al. Theorems 1.4/5.3 are the closest checked arbitrary-corruption upper bound; the present result closes their quarter-to-half gap, relative to cited versions.
At p=1/3 the present upper bound has the order of the cited logarithmic obstruction.
Repair benchmark, certificate minimization and preorder output build on Anand et al. Lemma 3.2 and Section 5.
The common-good-neighbor argument of Anand et al. Lemma 5.6 needs a good-pair fraction exceeding one half.
Positive density in every large disjoint rectangle plus order domination implies sum D_i <= (320r/eta)W+(8r/eta)M.
Hereditary rectangle density gives a star with r leaves in any 2 ceil(2r/eta) vertex set.
Cheap path edges sum to at most 64W; each expensive-edge interval has length D_i/32 with both endpoints within D_i/32 of each point it covers.
A matching of short and long overlapping edges creates an empty r-by-r rectangle, so overlap is at most 8r/eta.
Integrating overlap controls all scales with D_max<=M, including the vacuous 2r>n case.
The credited repair has failure <=(n-1) beta^(n-2) and unconditional E[X]<=2(1+4/alpha)M, alpha=(1-p)^2.
Fixed-p rational parameters and finite tree/rectangle enumeration give an observable deterministic algorithm, even with zeros or vacuous rectangles.
The uniform mask event has failure at most n^-12, uniformly over subsequent adversarial values and selected tree.
On E intersect F the repair tree qualifies and minimum observed cost is at most X; analysis graph density is at least eta.
The selected preorder has W<=2X and H-edge domination, yielding Y<=(320r/eta)(2X+M).
The good-event expectation is at most (320r/eta)(2B_p+1)M.
Every output has true cost <=(n-1)M, giving complementary expectation <=(1+2/alpha^3)M.
The explicit C_p is finite for fixed p<1/2, independent of aspect ratio and replacement magnitudes; averaging covers randomized adversaries.
The standard positive-distance two-cluster regularization preserves Anand et al. half-boundary obstruction, with expected crossing count 2ab/n and optimum 1+(n-2)delta.
Taking delta=n^-2 yields Omega(n) obstruction.
Exact checks covered 160 integer metrics at n=8,12,16,24 including nonuniform weights and zeros.
Exact checks covered 2,802,752 disjoint rectangles.
Exhaustive checks covered 33,866 pair masks for n=2,...,6 and p in {0,1/3,2/5,49/100}.
A separate model context reconstructed the proof and recomputed finite checks using a different implementation.
No polynomial/quasi-polynomial runtime or further application is established; constants deteriorate near one half.
